name: Philip Massinger
credit: Engraved portrait of Philip Massinger by Charles Grignion the Elder, c. 1750 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Philip Massinger (1583–1640), born at Salisbury and educated at Oxford, wrote or co-wrote some forty plays, among them A New Way to Pay Old Debts and The City Madam, and often collaborated with John Fletcher, Thomas Dekker and Nathaniel Field. He was buried in London in March 1640.

Bullen thought lyric verse was not Massinger's gift; the two songs here, from The Emperor of the East and The Guardian, are the ones he printed in Lyrics from the Dramatists of the Elizabethan Age (1889).

poems.title: Death Invoked
poems.author: Philip Massinger
poems.collection: Lyrics from the Dramatists of the Elizabethan Age, ed. A. H. Bullen (London: Nimmo, 1889)
poems.text:
Why art thou slow, thou rest of trouble, Death,
To stop a wretch's breath,
That calls on thee, and offers her sad heart
A prey unto thy dart?
I am nor young nor fair; be, therefore, bold:
Sorrow hath made me old,
Deformed, and wrinkled; all that I can crave
Is quiet in my grave.
Such as live happy, hold long life a jewel;
But to me thou art cruel,
If thou end not my tedious misery
And I soon cease to be.
Strike, and strike home, then; pity unto me,
In one short hour's delay, is tyranny.

poems.title: The Forest's Queen
poems.author: Philip Massinger
poems.collection: Lyrics from the Dramatists of the Elizabethan Age, ed. A. H. Bullen (London: Nimmo, 1889)
poems.text:
Welcome, thrice welcome to this shady green,
Our long-wished Cynthia, the forest's queen!
The trees begin to bud, the glad birds sing
In winter, changed by her into the spring.
We know no night,
Perpetual light
Dawns from your eye:
You being near,
We cannot fear,
Though death stood by.

From you our swords take edge, our hearts grow bold;
From you in fee their lives your liegemen hold.
These groves your kingdom, and our laws your will;
Smile, and we spare; but if you frown, we kill.

Bless then the hour
That gives the power
In which you may,
At bed and board,
Embrace your lord
Both night and day.

Welcome, thrice welcome to this shady green,
Our long-wished Cynthia, the forest's queen!
